seo.title: Ads in AI Mode: What Local Businesses Should Know
seo.meta_description: Google is expanding ads in AI Mode and launching multiturn ads in the U.S. How they work and what Anaheim and Orange County advertisers should do now.

h1: Ads in AI Mode: How Google's Sponsored Results Work for Local Businesses
answer: Google is expanding ads in AI Mode to more countries and launching multiturn ads in the U.S., so ads can appear in follow-up questions, always labeled Sponsored. Existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns are eligible automatically, and Google says paid ads don't influence the organic AI responses. Anaheim and Orange County advertisers should check targeting, assets and landing pages.
key_takeaways: Multiturn ads launching in the U.S. for follow-up questions.
Ads are labeled Sponsored and don't influence organic AI answers.
Existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns are eligible.
AI Mode queries are on average three times longer than traditional searches.

sections.heading: What Google announced
sections.body_html: On October 28, 2026, Shashi Thakur, Vice President and General Manager of Google Search Ads, announced that ads in AI Mode are expanding to new countries. Google is scaling them in Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and Singapore, with plans for more locales including Brazil, Mexico and the United Kingdom in the fourth quarter of 2026. In the U.S., Google is launching multiturn ads, which can appear in follow-up questions in AI Mode.

sections.heading: Why Google says this matters
sections.body_html: Google says that in AI Mode, queries are on average three times longer than traditional searches, citing its US AI Mode report from May 2026. Longer, conversational questions give Google more context about what someone needs. Google also says click-through rates are already similar between sponsored and organic product list items within AI Mode, based on its US internal data from late August to early September 2026.

sections.heading: Always labeled Sponsored
sections.body_html: Google's Ads help page says all ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode are clearly labeled Sponsored and visually distinguished from organic content. It also states that paid advertising does not influence the organic responses generated by Google AI. Paying for ads doesn't buy a mention in the AI answer itself.

sections.heading: No new campaigns needed
sections.body_html: Advertisers don't need new campaigns or separate budgets. Google says existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns are automatically eligible through the Google Ads auction. Text ads and Shopping ads can appear, and Google is experimenting with other formats such as local inventory ads and vehicle ads. Availability is in English in the U.S. and select English-speaking markets, expanding over time.

sections.heading: How ads are matched
sections.body_html: Google matches ads either directly to the query, when the search already shows commercial intent, or contextually to both the query and the AI response, when someone asks a longer, exploratory question. Google's example: someone asking why their pool is green may see ads for pool vacuums or algae treatment, because the AI answer mentions cleaning steps.

sections.heading: Which targeting is eligible
sections.body_html:
TargetingDirect query matchingContextual matching
AI Max for Search, broad match, Shopping, Performance MaxYesYes
Exact and phrase match keywordsYes, for clear commercial intentNo

Source: Google Ads Help. Advertisers who rely only on exact and phrase match won't appear in contextual placements on broader questions.

sections.heading: AI explainers
sections.body_html: Google says some placements may show AI explainers: short text generated by Gemini that explains how an ad relates to what the person is looking for. They can draw on the query, the AI response and publicly available sources, including your website. They aren't part of your headlines or descriptions, which makes accurate website content even more important.

sections.heading: What this means for local advertisers
sections.body_html: For a pool service in Anaheim, a dentist in Irvine or a contractor in Santa Ana, AI Mode questions are often detailed: costs, timing, comparisons. Ads can now follow the conversation. Your assets, landing pages and website content all shape how you're presented.

sections.heading: Checklist for this month
sections.body_html:
1. Review whether your campaigns use broad match, AI Max or Performance Max if you want contextual placements.
  2. Update headlines, descriptions, images and prices in your assets.
  3. Make landing pages answer the detailed questions customers ask.
  4. Check your website facts, since AI explainers may draw on it.
  5. Watch performance and lead quality, not just clicks.

sections.heading: Organic visibility still matters
sections.body_html: Because ads don't influence the organic AI response, being mentioned in the answer itself depends on the same things as before: clear, accurate pages, consistent listings and genuine reviews. Most businesses benefit from both: organic visibility for trust and ads for reach when budgets allow.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine a homeowner in Orange asking AI Mode how to fix a leaking water heater and whether to repair or replace it. A plumber running broad match or Performance Max could appear in a Sponsored section as the conversation turns to replacement costs. Meanwhile, a plumber whose website clearly explains repair versus replacement and lists prices has a better chance of being cited in the organic answer.

sections.heading: Measure carefully
sections.body_html: Track leads and booked jobs by campaign, not only clicks. Google's Invalid Traffic card can show what was filtered, but your own records show whether AI Mode traffic turns into customers.

sections.heading: Questions to ask your ads manager
sections.body_html:
• Which of our campaigns use broad match, AI Max or Performance Max, and which rely only on exact and phrase match?
  • Are our headlines, descriptions, images and prices current in every asset group?
  • Which landing page does each campaign send people to, and does it answer detailed questions?
  • How are we measuring leads and booked jobs, not just clicks?
  • What negative keywords keep us out of irrelevant conversations?

sections.heading: Budgets and expectations
sections.body_html: Because AI Mode placements come through existing campaigns, there is no separate budget to set. That also means spend can shift toward these placements without anyone noticing. Look at your search terms and placement reports regularly, compare cost per lead before and after you change targeting, and make one change at a time so you know what caused any difference. For a small business in Orange County with a limited budget, it is often better to keep tight targeting on your best services and expand only when the numbers justify it.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Ads in AI Mode are expanding, and in the U.S. they can now appear in follow-up questions. They're labeled Sponsored and don't influence organic answers. Anaheim and Orange County advertisers should review targeting, refresh assets and make sure their websites answer detailed questions.

faqs.q: What are ads in AI Mode?
faqs.a: Sponsored ads that can appear within or alongside AI Mode responses when a conversation has commercial relevance.

faqs.q: Do I need a new campaign for AI Mode ads?
faqs.a: No. Google says existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns are automatically eligible.

faqs.q: Do ads influence the AI answer?
faqs.a: No. Google says paid advertising doesn't influence organic responses generated by Google AI.
Ads that can appear in follow-up questions in AI Mode; Google is launching them in the U.S.

faqs.q: Do exact match keywords show in AI Mode?
faqs.a: For clear commercial queries, yes; they aren't eligible for contextual matching on broader questions.
Short Gemini-generated text explaining how an ad relates to the search, which can draw on your website.

faqs.q: How much longer are AI Mode searches?
faqs.a: Google says on average three times longer than traditional searches.

faqs.q: Do you work with businesses in Anaheim and Orange County?
faqs.a: Yes. Chimera is based in Anaheim, California and works with businesses across Orange County, California, from Anaheim and Santa Ana to Irvine and the coastal cities.
